title: Universal rank-one H0 gives a locally free first cokernel
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and P a cochain complex of R-modules. Suppose P^(-1)=0 and P^0 and P^1 are finitely generated projective R-modules. Suppose that for every commutative R-algebra B, the degree-zero homology of P tensor_R B is isomorphic to B as a B-module. Then for every prime ideal p of R, the localization at p of the R-module P^1 / im(d^0) is a free R_p-module.

source.place: Tags 00O0 and 00NX; rank-(n-1) unit-minor adaptation of 00O0, with the local-ring and residue-field H0 tests

proof.text: Since P^(-1)=0, after scalar extension H^0 identifies with the kernel of d^0. At a prime p, finite projectivity makes source and target finite free over A=R_p. The residue-field test gives source rank n at least one and matrix rank n-1. Choose a unit (n-1)-minor and eliminate its rows and columns, obtaining diag(id_(n-1),g) where g:A -> A^m. The same row and column operations preserve kernels. This is the unit-minor argument of Tag 00O0 applied to the maximal nonzero residue block, not an application of its injectivity assertion to d.

The A-algebra test gives ker(g) isomorphic to A. Compose an isomorphism A -> ker(g) with the inclusion ker(g) -> A: this is multiplication by c and is injective. For each entry b of g one has bc=0, hence cb=0, hence b=0 by injectivity. Thus g=0. The cokernel of diag(id,g) is A^m and is free. Exactness of localization identifies this cokernel with the localization of P^1/im(d^0). The n=1 case uses the empty minor; there are no primes for the zero ring.
